asr.text: Reyes, Dale, the logbook should be in front of you.
I headed out early. The service folder is on the desk under the work order.
The first survey is routine. Check calibration before you let it run.
Did you get something to eat?
Good, better than trying to live on the coffee here.
I tried that once, wouldn't recommend it.
There are crackers in the bottom drawer, still in the wrapper.
No promises about the coffee. It was here when I came in.
Start with the log. I've marked what's done and what's left for you.
Bank 3 has two amber indicators. Amber is normal. Write it down if that changes.
Your folder lists the local service records and the radio schedule. Get the dated copies. We need something to check our clocks against.
Operations office is locked. The papers for tonight are already on your desk.
Ward is on call for the morning run. She wants observations, she can sign, not our best guess.
You can reach me on the service line. If something doesn't fit the log, call before you throw anything away.
Alright, have a good shift!
Dale, you have the service sheet?
Then, start with the feeder marked on that sheet. A receiver warning and a supply fault are two different things.
The junction station is down the short gravel turnoff. Leave the truck outside the service gate.
Use the service check on the cabinet. Note what the affected light does, not just what the indicator says.
There should be one clear result. If the result is not clear, leave it unresolved and call me.
I hear you. Check the cabinet label against the service sheet.
If they match, run the check and watch the light at the far end.
Write down the result and the time. Keep that for the next check.
Dale, what did it actually print?
Minus 39 on the paper.
Keep the original. Put the clock reading beside it before you do anything else.
Do not correct the number, just because it looks wrong.
I've seen numbers that shouldn't have come out of that solver.
I haven't worked out why, I kept the records.
Keep yours too, we can argue about the explanation later.
Check your inspection card. Put the test time beside the new printout.
If you've cleared the supply fault, compare that time with this one.
Alright, put the paper somewhere safe.
Call me if the next observation disagrees with the first one.
You found a spare.
I should have told you there was more than a service folder.
What are you looking at?
What once a result somebody else can repeat, she's right too.
asr.review: unresolved: 'Ward wants' heard as 'What once' (German W as V); seed 42-44 had one edit, seed 47 three: retake at 42 in the next GPU window, then listen.

asr.text: I had clippings, bad frames and people who remembered different nights.
I kept the lot until I could put two observations on the same page.
Watch the pole, not the patch.
The patch could be a recording fault. The poll gives you a fixed reference.
asr.review: accepted: homophone pole/poll, as in the Evening pack's D31_TAPE_002; all other words exact.

asr.text: Use the field sheet. I marked the camera position.
I haven't worked through those survey files.
The folder in my office is my own. I haven't changed an old report.
Keep the originals together, check whose name is on the signed copy.
Start with one thing you can check. Take a photograph from the same place.
And don't take my word for something just because I wrote it down.
Say that again. The service result and the light disagree.
You checked the ordinary supply, the backup and the indicator?
Good. Write down every check you made. Keep that separate from what you think caused it.
Bring the record back to Zaro, Ward will need to read it.
asr.review: accepted: station name SARO transcribed as 'Zaro'.

asr.text: Reyes, I'm here.
If you've got witness statements, keep their exact words with the record.
Give Ward what you've actually checked. Leave the rest marked uncertain.
Call me when you get back in.
Check the survey reference before the unattended run. Write down anything you have to change, even if it fixes itself.
The camera is beside the east door. Take a reference before you touch the fault.
And try your way out while the lights are good. A door on a plan is no use if you have never opened it.
The complaint is about the inspection lamp, just that lamp.
Use the marked service control outside the fence. Leave the locked equipment alone.
Watch the lamp and the indicator separately. Tell me whether they agree.
The service drawer has a spare, brass tag, office, I should have put it in the handover.
Take the field folder. I wrote down where I stood so somebody else could try it.
I saw the same shape from two places. I do not know whether it was looking at me.
What? No wait, the station line. So you are the new one. You have four minutes, I have a soldering iron in my hand and I am not putting it down for you.
What is on the card? It is printed, somebody typed it so that I would not have to say it to you on the telephone.
Point, tune, record, register file. Amber is normal. If the amber changes you write it down, you do not have a feeling about it. Nobody has ever fixed a receiver with a feeling.
Half. You went and counted or you are guessing. No. Do not tell me. Count them. Then the outer branches in the order on the sheet not in the order you like.
And when you finish, you put my tools back where they were. Himmel, where they were, I will know.
No.
I said, no, is this the service line, then you ask me about service.
It is a list. I sent somebody to look for a pump in somebody's fence. That is what that was. A pump.
Then you leave them wired where they are. They are good tags, dated, initialed, one-to-a-stop. Do you know how rare that is in this county? Do you?
Leave them.
Alone. In that truck with those brakes and at what hour? Verdammt. Did you touch it?
Then you have learned nothing and it cost you a tank of gas. Stay off that flat. I do not need another form to fill in.
Every night, about the coffee, about a lamp, Reyes would read me the same number twice because it was funny and it was not funny.
There is a message on my machine. I have played it one time.
It said what it said. You are not going to hear it. Go and point your antennas.
You wrote down when it starts, when it stops, then you have two numbers, which is two more than you had, nine. I do not want to hear what you think it was.
asr.review: accepted: German 'Nein' transcribed as English 'nine'; all other words exact.

asr.text: Sleep in the building tonight. Door shut. That is not an order. Nobody here can give you an order, apparently.
Because the telephone rings. What kind of question is that? Somebody at that station calls at night and somebody picks up. That is how it is supposed to work.
Have you eaten? There are crackers in the bottom drawer, still in the wrapper. You did not hear it from me.
So hang them. Go. Everybody goes. I have worked with people who could not find their own feet with both hands and they all had somewhere better to be.
Not on hook one, any other hook, hook one you leave.
You call the service line about paper? I sign for parts. Ward signs for paper. Ask Ward.
Then the answer is the same, only louder, not in my drawer, not on my bench, ask Ward.
Dale Field Maintenance, you are the new one. Amber is normal. Do not touch Bank 3. I do not care who you are. Dale out.
One job filed, I will alert the newspapers. Now the next one.
Who told you to go in that locker? Nobody, that is who. Leave the mug where it is.
You are out on my survey now? Nobody asked you. You read the text, you do not add to them. Dale out.
asr.review: unresolved: 'tags' heard as 'text' in seeds 42-47: listen.

asr.text: It is after 2. Are you in the building? Do not tell me about the sky. Be in the building.
You mended a branch. I looked at the line from here. It is a clean joint. Genau. That is the first thing anyone has done right out there since April. Do not get used to me saying it.
Ten jobs, Ward told me. I did not ask her to. It is almost competent. Keep going.
Your log has a hole in it. You put a time on each end of it in ink, and then you call me, not before Mench.
Twice now, what told me? One more and they give your knights to somebody else. After dark you stay in the building. Verstanden?
asr.review: unresolved: 'Ward told me' heard as 'what told me' (German W), nights/knights; seed 43 had one edit: retake at 43 in the next GPU window, then listen.

asr.text: Three days towards assessment. She reads numbers. I have seen your numbers. Stop looking out the window and file something.
asr.review: unresolved: 'to Ward's' heard as 'towards' (German W); every seed 42-47 the same: listen for whether the name is clear.

asr.text: The deputy called my bench, somebody has been out at wagon 23, he says, and he has an idea who leave that one to the county.
Somebody saw you out at the mine on the west side. That is as far as you go. Not in. Not for a list. Not for anybody. Dale out.
You are still on nights, they had a pool on you at the district, I said three days. Now I owe a man in Socorro five dollars.
So she kept us. I ran the whole array up and down from my bench to see if it still moves. It moves. Do not get used to it. Dale out.
Your chart has a burst on it at 10 to 1. 10 to 1. Who keeps appointments in this county? You run the control, then you file, not the other way.
You are asking around Kallig after somebody who is not at their post? The county rang my bench. You are the station, not the county. Write what you saw.
asr.review: accepted: place name Caliche transcribed as 'Kallig'.

asr.text: You walked out on their raked ground, do not tell me. Write down how wide the circle was and the time and do not go back. Verstanden?
Somebody in Kallich is not at their post, the county says. People go to Belen, people come back, you do your card and you lock the door. Dale out.
asr.review: accepted: place name Caliche transcribed as 'Kallich'.

asr.text: The deputy drove past wagon 23. Somebody has been in it since April, he says, and wiped the dash. Not him, not the district. You stay off that flat. Dale out.
A week towards numbers. I have shut the pool at the district. Nobody would take the other side of it. Do not make me open it again. Dale out.
asr.review: unresolved: 'to Ward's' heard as 'towards' (German W); every seed the same: listen.

asr.text: Their van is out there with the door open. The deputy says, you do not go and close it. You write down where and you stay in the building.
Helicopter low over the land this morning and two cars that are not the counties you did not see them No, you write down that you did with the time.
asr.review: accepted: homophone county's/counties; all other words exact.

asr.text: The attendant says you have the thermos from Unit 23, tag it and put it in the outgoing tray. The district runs it to Socorro. Do not drink from it, Mensch.
You were out at Wagon 23 again, reading the dash, the deputy read it in April. He wrote down the number and not one word of what he thought. Do the same.
The county inspector wrote to you? He wrote to my bench too. He wants to know whether the array moves. I said ask the operator, so make it move.
You let the people with the van into my station? They read my logbooks. I know, because the logbooks are in order now and they never are.
You filed an assessment, now the county reads it and rings my bench to ask what it means and I say ask the operator. Do not make me a liar.
Two weeks and half my array is still lying on its back. Ward reads that line first, the county second, and I read it every morning, meant something.
asr.review: unresolved: 'Mend something' heard as 'meant something' in seeds 42-47: listen.

asr.text: Saro Knight, this is Dale. Come in.
Night operator, I know you have the set. Come in.
Nothing fine, then it goes on a slip by the phone, Dale out.
Finally, next time you answer the first time.
Again, what? Nothing? Then take your thumb off the button. Dale out!
That is four times today. Four. I am turning my set to the wall. Call the service line in the morning. Dale out.
Now you call. I called you before on channel 1, you keep it on 1 and when I call you answer, Dale out.
You are driving and talking on my channel, both hands on the wheel, out.
You sound wrong. Both times are in the log? Good. Tonight you stay in the building. Dale out.
At this hour, you are inside? Good. Stay in. You do not open the door to look at anything, Dale, out.
After two and you are outside, nine, I do not want to know why. Go in now, they're loud.
asr.review: unresolved: 'Dale out' heard as 'they're loud'; seed 42 had one edit, seed 47 three: retake at 42 in the next GPU window, then listen.

asr.text: Do you know what time it is? I know what time it is. Is something on fire? No? Then write it in the log. Dale out.
I am up a pole in the sun with a meter in my teeth. Call the service line like a person. Dale out.
You are standing next to a telephone. A telephone. Use the card, use the telephone and leave my channel alone.
Antennas down and you call me? The sheet has the order. Read the sheet then mend them. Dale out.
Where are you out there with my truck? You bring it back with four tires and gas in it. Dale out.
What? Is it the amber lamps? The amber is normal. Do the card. Dale out.
The county put a call through to my bench, so now it is your problem.
I am not driving out there. Dale out.
Leave the array where it is until I have read the encoders myself. And if you go out there, you go by daylight and you take the walkie. Out.
Saddle, Dale, pick up.
asr.review: unresolved: SARO heard as 'Saddle' (best of seeds 42-47): listen.

asr.text: Saro, the walkie-now.
Fine, I leave it on the slip by the phone.
